title: All in One and One for All: A Simple yet Effective Method towards Cross-domain Graph Pretraining

problem.claim: Applying cross-domain pretraining to graphs is challenging because it often results in negative transfer, especially in few-shot learning scenarios where external knowledge is needed.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for an approach that can leverage commonalities across diverse graph datasets while avoiding negative transfer in target tasks.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Graph COordinators for PrEtraining (GCOPE), an approach that harnesses commonalities across diverse graph datasets to enhance few-shot learning.
GCOPE provides a unification framework that amalgamates disparate graph datasets during pretraining to distill and transfer knowledge to target tasks.
The authors report experiments across multiple graph datasets evaluating the efficacy of their approach.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GCOPE as a novel approach and characterize the work as a pioneering contribution to graph foundational models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across multiple graph datasets and claim superior efficacy for their approach.
The authors report that their method leverages the synergistic potential of multiple graph datasets for pretraining.
The authors state that code is available at the provided GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract frames multi-domain training and broad generalization as successful paradigms for large language models.
It states that transferring these ideas to graphs is difficult because cross-domain pretraining can cause negative transfer, particularly in few-shot learning.
The paper introduces GCOPE and a unification framework for combining graph datasets and transferring distilled knowledge to target tasks.
The authors report superior efficacy in experiments across multiple graph datasets and present the work as a pioneering graph foundational-model contribution.
The abstract provides a link to the code repository.

source_observation.claim: Cross-domain pretraining can produce negative transfer when graph datasets differ substantially.

interpretation.claim: Combining heterogeneous datasets requires mechanisms that identify and exploit shared structure rather than assuming unrestricted transfer is beneficial.

application.claim: For few-shot graph learning, consider a pretraining design that explicitly models commonalities across datasets before transferring knowledge to target tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the proposed transfer strategy succeeds or fails across particular graph domains or task types.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training objectives, or coordination mechanism used by GCOPE.
The abstract does not identify the graph datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the conditions under which negative transfer is avoided.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported efficacy.
